parts.text: A student determines the density of modelling clay by two methods. Method 1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Fig. 1.1 shows one face of a piece of modelling clay that the student uses. This is sample A. Fig. 1.1 The student measures the depth d of sample A. d = .......................................................... cm 3.2

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Measure and record the length l and the width w of the sample A of modelling clay. Fig. 1.1 is drawn actual size. l = .......................................................... cm w = .......................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the volume V A of sample A using the equation V A = l × w × d . V A = ................................................... cm 3 [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Fig. 1.2 shows sample A on a balance. Record the mass m A of sample A to the nearest g. Fig. 1.2 m A = ...................................................... g [1]

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Calculate the density ρ A of sample A of modelling clay using the equation ρ A = m A V A . Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this method and include the unit. ρ A = ......................................................... [2] Method 2

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student records the volume V 1 of water in a measuring cylinder. V 1 = ........................................................ cm 3 He carefully lowers sample B of the same modelling clay into the measuring cylinder until it is completely covered with water. He records the new reading V 2 of the water level in the measuring cylinder. V 2 = ........................................................ cm 3 150 182

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate the volume V B of sample B using the equation V B = V 2 – V 1 . V B = .................................................. cm 3 [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The student measures the mass m B of sample B. m B = ............................................................ g Calculate the density ρ B of sample B using the equation ρ B = m B V B . Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this method and include the unit. ρ B = ......................................................... [1] 60

ms.text:
Statement to match results.
Justification to match results and to include the idea of within (or beyond) the limits of experimental accuracy.

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Tick the boxes that describe the correct line of sight for taking a reading of the volume of water in a measuring cylinder. Fig. 1.3 shows the curved surface of water, which is called the meniscus. Fig. 1.3 along the scale parallel to the scale perpendicular to the scale vertical to the scale in line with the bottom of the meniscus in line with the top of the meniscus in line with midway between the top and bottom of the meniscus.
